div.head: I Cn 2.2
div.ab: Þonne is swiðe rihtlic, þæt Godes ciricgrið binnon wagum ⁊ Cristenes ciningces handgrið stande æfre [efen] unwemme; ⁊ se ðe aðor fulbrece, þolige landes ⁊ lifes, butan se ciningc gearian wylle.
Ðonne is swiðe rihtlic, þæt Godes cyricgrið binnan wagum ⁊ Crystenes cyninges handgrið stande efen unwemmed; and se þe aðor fulbrece, ðolige landes ⁊ lifes, buton him se cyningc gearian wylle.
Ðonne is swiðe rihtlic, þæt Godes ciricgrið binnon wágum ⁊ Cristenes cynges handgrið stande efen unwæmme.

Et ualde iustum est, ut ęcclesię pax intra parietes suos et pax Christiani regis, quam manu sua dederit, semper inuiolata (inconuulsa) permaneat; quicumque alterutram perfregerit, de uita et omnibus in misericordia regis sit.
Þonne is swiðe rihtlic, þæt Godes ciricgrið binnon wagum ⁊ Cristenes ciningces handgrið stande æfre unwemme; ⁊ se ðe aðor fulbrece þolige landes ⁊ lifes, butan [him] se ciningc gearian wille.
Þonne is swiðe rihtlic þæt Godes ciricgrið binnon wagum and Cristenes ciningces handgrið stande æfre unwemme; and se ðe aðor fulbrece þolige landes and lifes, butan him se ciningc gearian wylle.

Nun ist höchst rechtmässig, dass der von Gottes Kirche innerhalb ihrer Mauern [ausgehende] Sonderschutz und der Sonderschutz aus der Hand des christlichen Königs gleichermassen (stets G) unverletzlich bestehe; und wer einen von beiden gänzlich [durch Todtschlag] verletzt, verliere Land und Leben, ausser wenn ihn der König begnadigen will.

Now it is very right that the protection of God's church within its walls and the protection given by the Christian king's own hand stand equally (always, G) inviolate; and whoever wholly breaks either [by killing], let him lose land and life, unless the king is willing to pardon him.

Therefore it is very right and proper that the protection given by the church of God within its walls, and the protection granted by a Christian king in person should always remain inviolate; and he who violates either of them shall lose both land and life, unless the king is willing to pardon him.

Accordingly, it is most proper that the sanctuary within the walls of God’s church and the protection received from the Christian king’s hand remain always inviolate; and the person who defies either of them shall forfeit land and life unless the king is willing to pardon him.
